header: THE INTRODUCTION TO THE SEARCH BAR, at the top of the user guide, for a new user: what the bar is, what it can be asked, and what it cannot (yet). One data file, read by src/components/help/SearchBarIntro.tsx. I made it follow the bar as it is drawn (23 Nov 2026): the two rows of buttons under the box. AREAS is the first row, "Search in", button by button in the bar's own order; MORE_TOOLS is the second row. When you add a button to the bar (src/records/domains.ts), add ONE new item in AREAS here; the guide's test (searchBarIntro.selftest.ts) fails until you do, so the introduction cannot fall behind the bar.

doc: How to get started, in three steps.

behaviours: the list is the first row of the bar, in its order: Everything, then every choice of src/records/domains.ts
the row titles are those the bar draws
Everything is the button the bar starts on, where the site and department links appear as you type
People has one part for each of the bar's three ways, under the bar's own names, and says which need no AI
People by name or number: ticket, CUG mobile (or the last 4 digits of an executive's), SAIL personal number when signed in, a different spelling still finds the person, with or without the department
People by department and by asking: two lists, seniority order, what it understood; counts, who is in charge, the count by designation, seniority, comparisons

PAX says the nearest related entries are shown with their numbers when the place is not listed; Hospital OPD says the department names are buttons; Holidays and Degrees say what they hold (the level of a degree, the PhD holders, the doctors' degrees)
Circulars & Notices: by title, by the answer inside, an announcement by what its PDF says, the answer names the document and opens it, and a word in no document is said
every area has a name and a detail, and none is listed twice

four rules: Everything is the start and every way back lands on it (with the suggestion dot); a chosen button never goes on to the circulars and says nothing was found; the examples under the row; the box is cleared on another button
the rules say what the code does: the box is wiped, a chosen button never reaches the circulars, the bar says it found nothing
the second row's pointers name the two buttons of the bar: Utility Services and Executive Deep Search

the Admin pointer names the third button of More tools and says: signed out it asks first (Are you authorised to access them?), Yes opens sign-in and then the authority is checked, No returns to Everything, an authorised person gets the admin home page and anyone else a red message

the Executive Deep Search pointer says: several circulars read together, one written summary with its circulars, signed-in executives, anyone else is asked first, Yes opens sign-in, and the Deep search (EDS) tab tells all
nothing else of the deep search is on this tab (no 'briefing', no 'Deep Synthesis', no score or model), and no Good-to-know point is about it
${text} ${EDS_POINTER.after} ${CHOICE_RULES.join(" ")}
no Utility Service is listed among the buttons of the first row (each is on the Utility Services tab)

the Utility Services pointer says they help employees in different ways, are auxiliary, open from the button under More tools on a page of their own with Back, and have a tab of their own with the words that open each
it says what the bar is, and how to start in three steps (click, press where to look, type and press Enter)
the lead says that under the box are two rows (Search in, More tools) and that the bar's main work is finding things in the plant's own records
it says plainly that plant production data cannot be answered yet, that AI can be wrong, and that the management pages are the HOD's to open

the notes of this tab are the three general ones; the notes about the services (prices, shares, steel, flights, trains, fares, PIN codes, inflation, DA, PF, calculators) are on the Utility Services tab
no 'Good to know' point is long: each is under 400 characters
